key_insight: FL4N represents dynamic 3D scenes in a unified latent space rather than with explicit 4D primitives. The paper presents it as the first feed-forward latent model for synthesizing views across both camera positions and time.
problem_solved: Rendering a dynamic scene from new viewpoints and timestamps requires understanding both 3D structure and motion. Existing monocular feed-forward methods often use explicit 4D Gaussians, which can produce temporal inconsistencies and severe rendering artifacts.
method: Use a feed-forward model for 4D novel view synthesis from monocular input.
Encode a 4D scene prior in a unified latent representation instead of explicit 4D primitives.
Support rendering across viewpoints and timestamps; further architectural details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: FL4N offers an alternative to explicit Gaussian-based representations for dynamic-scene rendering. It targets temporal consistency and rendering quality, although the provided abstract includes no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: monocular input → unified 4D latent representation → novel views at different times.
Viewpoint-by-time grid illustrating the two dimensions of 4D novel view synthesis.
Conceptual comparison of explicit 4D Gaussian primitives and a unified latent scene representation.
Timeline of rendered frames highlighting temporal consistency as a key goal.
paper_title: FL4N: Feed-forward Latent Model for 4D Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Eunbeen Hong, Hyeonseo Yu, Honggyu An, Jooho Son, Hyunah Ko
